name: MorphoSwarm — open problems work queue

colour_rule.possible_pathway: pooled Delphi bridge posterior >= 15% (classification only — NOT green)
colour_rule.note: Shade bands show the range of opinion. Green is reserved for >70% (light) and >80% (dark); a posterior in the teens is burnt orange. Panel range per problem is in viability.panel_range_percent.

protocol: Pick one OP id; do not work two on the same branch without noting it.
Pre-register the attempt (hypotheses + scoring) before touching held-out data, following the repo's hash-locked blind-test contract.

RECORD A PROBABILITY FOR EVERY ACTION before attempting it (edge prob 0-100 + probNote with method and date, Thompson-registry style); after the attempt, update the target node's status and never edit the recorded prob. The graph builder refuses edges with neither a prob nor an explicit probStatus.
Report negative results as results; pruned branches stay in the graph.
Close by updating the source documents and re-running docs/build_problem_graph_html.py, whose self-checks must pass.

problems.title: Prize 1 — close the transparent-gate loophole (short runs 1≤a_i≤7)
problems.gap: Defects D1(t)=1 are proved to arrive infinitely often, but not proved to ever land on a closed gate {c_t=1}. Depth-1 right cylinder has positive topological entropy (~0.32 bits/step) on short runs, so no deeper local transducer closes this; it needs a global phase-spreading / mixing invariant.
problems.done: A proof (ideally Lean-checked) that for all t0, Π and short-run words, some D1(t)=1 lands on {c_t=1} — or a counterexample word, which would be just as valuable.

problems.title: TOP-07 · When does continuous reaction-diffusion collapse to a discrete automaton? Meinhardt mantle PDE vs the Lean-proved Rule 30 gate
problems.gap: Ocellated lizard scales behave as a cellular automaton emerging from RD on a thick-skin lattice (Manukyan 2017), and the repo has Lean-proved that the Ermentrout-Oster neural mantle gate is bit-for-bit Rule 30 — but whether the repo's Meinhardt-Klingler Conus PDE, discretised at the mantle, induces a Rule 30-class local rule has never been measured. It is the bridge between the Rule 30 programme and the RD programme, and the RD-vs-neural shell-pattern debate is still molecularly unresolved.
problems.done: From a Meinhardt PDE kymograph at the mantle edge, extract the empirical 3-neighbourhood -> next-state transducer table (binary threshold pre-registered), report the fraction of transitions agreeing with Rule 30 vs Rule 90 vs best-fit rule, plus the 2D ANF-carry density and wall chirality already used to separate R30 from R90 (node r0); verdict thresholds locked before running.

gemini-4-argon.label: Gemini 4 Argon Medium
gemini-4-argon.note: The crux is fundamental symmetry: Meinhardt-Klingler's 1D diffusion operator d^2/dx^2 is reflection-symmetric (left-right invariant), whereas Rule 30 breaks left-right symmetry via a_{i-1} XOR (a_i OR a_{i+1}). Thus the transducer test will reach a fast, decisive verdict—almost certainly proving that isotropic Meinhardt PDE reduces to a symmetric elementary CA class (like Rule 90/18) rather than chiral Rule 30 unless oblique wave travel or asymmetric coupling is present.

claude-fable-5-1.note: Crux: a symmetric PDE should map to a symmetric (Rule 90-like or additive) rule, so expect a decisive negative on Rule 30; lock the coarse-graining scale and threshold in the registry before running.

problems.title: TOP-09 · Turing's neglected case: is there a wave (Turing-Hopf) dispersion signature in the embryonic Ca2+ wave field?
problems.gap: Turing 1952 also derived oscillatory, travelling-wave instabilities; essentially no developmental system has been shown to use one. The repo's Ca2+ spark-track data (x, y, t per event) is the only place here that can ask whether an observed wave field carries a dispersion ridge omega(k) distinct from a single driven front (omega = v k).
problems.done: A pre-registered space-time spectral test on existing spark_tracks CSVs: estimate the (k, omega) power surface per embryo, fit the driven-front line, and test for a secondary ridge against phase-randomised surrogates at a locked false-positive rate; report per-embryo outcomes and the pooled verdict either way.

problems.title: TOP-03 · The fine-tuning objection: replicate the two-node vs three-node Turing parameter-volume ratio and the 1%-uncertainty retention claim
problems.gap: Turing instability is topologically common but occupies tiny parameter volumes: 0.00035% of sampled space for the classical two-node circuit vs 0.022% for the best three-node topology (Tica et al. 2024, Latin-hypercube linear stability), with 33% retention under 1% parameter uncertainty around a Turing I point. These numbers decide whether the fine-tuning objection to biological Turing systems stands; they have not been independently reproduced.
problems.done: A pre-registered Latin-hypercube linear-stability sweep on the repo's two-node kinetics and a three-node immobile-node topology within published parameter bounds, reporting both Turing fractions and the 1%/5% local-retention fractions; verdict = within one order of magnitude of the published ratio (>=10x three-node over two-node) or not.

problems.title: TOP-01 · Mechanism identification: a pre-registered statistic that separates reaction-diffusion from colonisation, phase separation and buckling on static patterns
problems.gap: Pattern phenomenology does not identify mechanism: zebrafish stripes are cell-contact mediated (Nakamasu 2009), feather buds mechanical first (Shyer 2017), Holstein spotting indistinguishable between growing RD and Eden colonisation at p=0.91 (OP-11). No registered discriminator exists that, given only an adult pattern, says which class of generator made it with a stated error rate.
problems.done: A hash-locked discriminator (candidate features: radial power-spectrum shape, Minkowski functionals, defect/junction statistics, two-point anisotropy) trained and scored on synthetic ground truth from four generators (Gray-Scott/Schnakenberg RD, Eden colonisation, Cahn-Hilliard phase separation, elastic buckling) with a pre-registered held-out accuracy threshold and published confusion matrix; then applied blind to the 10 coat-masked Holstein specimens, reported either way.

problems.title: TOP-02 · The diffusion-ratio problem: which molecularly identified Turing systems can be two-species at all?
problems.gap: Two-species activator-inhibitor models need D_inh/D_act above the Lean-checked threshold (d_c = 3.93 for the repo's Gray-Scott Jacobian; ~4-10 generally), yet measured extracellular diffusivities rarely show it; three-node networks with an immobile node remove the requirement (Marcon 2016) and extracellular wiring changes behaviour qualitatively (2025 bioRxiv). Nobody has tabulated, system by system, which of the molecularly supported cases (WNT/DKK, FGF/Shh palate, Bmp-Sox9-Wnt digits, GDF5/NOG joints, EDAR/WNT/BMP ridges, Nodal/Lefty) actually satisfies the two-species condition with measured D.
problems.done: A registered table of >=6 molecular Turing systems giving measured or bounded D_act, D_inh (with DOI), run through the repo's dispersion relation, classifying each as two-node-feasible / needs immobile third node / D unmeasured; the count in each class pre-registered before the literature values are looked up.

gemini-4-argon.label: Gemini 4 Argon Medium
gemini-4-argon.note: The crux is distinguishing truly unmeasured in vivo diffusivities from indirect effective range estimates, since all three classification buckets are already guaranteed to be populated by Nodal/Lefty, Bmp-Sox9-Wnt, and WNT/DKK. Note that d_c = 3.9271 is specific to Turing's 1952 numerical Jacobian example, whereas each biological system has its own kinetic Jacobian bounds on D_inh/D_act.

registered_prediction_followups.note: Registered predictions scored partially_resolved on 2026-10-26: outcome neither confirmed nor refuted; each names the exact missing series. Closing one means supplying that series, not re-arguing the prediction.

items.missing_evidence: Lipidation is functional in zebrafish Shh signalling: 'New chemical probes targeting cholesterylation of Sonic Hedgehog in human cells and zebrafish' (2014, doi:10.1039/C4SC01600A), and dual-lipid release biology reviewed in doi:10.1002/bies.202100133. Bound established: wild-type ShhNp is dually lipidated and tethered (repo state), and cholesterylation is required for normal signalling in zebrafish. NOT established from sources extracted: the specific registered gradient-shape claim (distal ptc-domain expansion + reduced near-source peak upon lipidation loss) in a zebrafish tissue assay. Missing data: paired ptc1/ptc2 domain measurements for lipidation-perturbed vs wild-type zebrafish Shh.

Bound established: the proportional architecture (clock period sets somite size at a given wavefront speed) is the standard, literature-supported segmentation-clock framework (zebrafish clock-mechanism studies, e.g. doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.0050150; core-circuit dynamics doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1001364). NOT established: a paired dataset (measured T change + measured S change, wavefront controlled) sufficient to test the registered x0.80/x0.90/x1.10/x1.20 multipliers within 5 points. Missing data: paired her1-period and somite-length measurements under a controlled-wavefront perturbation, tabulated in one source.

Bound established: 3.813 is the established vertex-model jamming value carried by the dataset law. NOT established: a zebrafish (EVL/epiboly) measured shape-index transition inside 3.76-3.87; the targeted literature search returned no zebrafish shape-index transition dataset. Missing data: cell shape-index series across a zebrafish epithelial jamming/unjamming transition (measurable from published epiboly images, not yet tabulated).

Bound established: insect tracheal systems are not generically Murray-optimal (ant tracheal branching violates network-transport assumptions, doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1007853; Murray compliance varies by insect system, doi:10.1186/s12915-021-01130-0), consistent with the negative prediction. NOT established: a Drosophila tracheal parent/daughter diameter series sufficient to fit an exponent against the registered 2.8-3.2 band. Missing data: tabulated Drosophila tracheal diameters across branch orders.

Bound established: Xenopus somitogenesis uses a her/hes segmentation clock with a wavefront, so the proportional S~T architecture is the applicable framework (cross-species replication target of ZF-CLK-01). NOT established: paired Xenopus period-manipulation + somite-length measurements sufficient to test the x0.80-x1.20 multipliers within 5 points. Missing data: paired clock-period and somite-length series under controlled wavefront conditions in Xenopus.

live_arguments.note: Contested literature questions (≥2 camps) mapped to repo datasets, genome tiers and the measurement that would settle each. Candidates only: Delphi-score the probability (recorded on the graph edge), then register, then score. Settled halves (e.g. LA-01) must not be re-litigated.

items.question: How is the zebrafish BMP dorsoventral gradient formed: Chordin-mediated shuttling, regulated free diffusion/source-sink, or ECM/HSPG-shaped diffusion?
items.settling_measurement: Paired FRAP/effective-mobility measurements of tagged BMP and Chordin plus pSmad1/5 gradient ranges in at least two Danio species of different embryo size, under identical staging.

items.question: Are zebrafish stripes (and fish pigment patterns generally) a Turing reaction-diffusion system, or a cell-interaction network that only mimics one?
items.settling_measurement: Stripe wavelength and regeneration kinetics in cell-interaction mutants (leopard/gja5b, pfeffer/csf1ra) compared quantitatively against both model classes fitted on the same fish; the Turing account must predict the wavelength shift from a kinetic parameter, the cell account from interaction ranges.

items.question: Is vertebrate digit patterning a BMP-SOX9-WNT Turing system modulated by Hox dose, or a positional-gradient system in which Turing-like periodicity is secondary?
items.settling_measurement: Digit wavelength (condensation spacing) as a function of distal Hox dose in allelic series, tested against the BSW prediction that wavelength -- not just digit identity -- shifts continuously with Hox-modulated parameters.

items.question: How is Hedgehog transported: extracellular diffusion (with Dispatched/Scube hand-off) or cytoneme-mediated delivery?
items.settling_measurement: Gradient range after cytoneme disruption that leaves secretion intact (and vice versa), in the same tissue, with the lipidation state of the transported species verified from sequence/protein state.

items.question: Does somite size scale with segmentation-clock period via wavefront speed (clock-and-wavefront), and what sets the scaling across species?
items.settling_measurement: Paired clock-period and somite-length measurements with PSM length/wavefront speed recorded in the same embryos, across at least the fish and frog systems the repo holds.

items.question: How does the Dpp/BMP gradient scale with the growing Drosophila wing disc: degradation-mediated scaling, expansion-repression, or growth-coupled production?
items.settling_measurement: Dpp gradient length, disc size, Dpp turnover and candidate-expander expression measured across growth stages/genotypes in one quantitative series; the two camps predict different couplings between turnover and length.

items.question: Is the bioelectric (Vmem) prepattern instructive for Xenopus craniofacial/orientation patterning -- upstream information that biochemical gradients read out -- or a downstream correlate of conventional pathways?
items.settling_measurement: Blinded, pre-registered ion-channel misexpression with BMP-pathway transcriptional readout and craniofacial scoring, where the bioelectric account predicts the readout change in advance and the conventional account predicts none without direct pathway manipulation. The repo's own blind-test contract (hash-locked, scorer refuses on mismatch) is the required format, given its earlier negative blind results.
